text:
alice_support: Hi @bob_customer_sre — saw your ticket about repeated 500s on KMS calls from your private deployment. You mentioned TLS timeouts and some key fetch errors. Can you paste the exact error from the Redwood agent logs?

bob_customer_sre: here's the truncated error from the agent on the application host:
```
2026-02-28T14:12:03Z ERROR redwood.agent.kms: key fetch failed: tls: handshake timeout
2026-02-28T14:12:03Z WARN  redwood.agent.kms: retrying key fetch (attempt 3)
2026-02-28T14:12:08Z ERROR redwood.agent.kms: key fetch failed: dial tcp 10.12.34.56:443: i/o timeout
```
I can reproduce locally from one of our app nodes.

alice_support: thanks. A couple suspects: (1) DNS resolving the KMS/HSM endpoint to a public IP (split-horizon DNS misconfig), (2) firewall/NAT dropping egress to the HSM on 443, or (3) TLS SNI mismatch (HSM expects specific SNI). Can you run these quick checks on one of the failing hosts and paste outputs?

- `dig +short kms.internal.example`
- `openssl s_client -connect 10.12.34.56:443 -servername kms.internal.example -showcerts`
- `curl -v --resolve 'kms.internal.example:443:10.12.34.56' https://kms.internal.example/health`
- `sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 10.12.34.56 and port 443 -c 50`

bob_customer_sre: ran them, outputs below. `dig` returns our private VIP: `10.12.34.56`. `curl` hangs with TLS handshake timeout. `openssl` output shows server cert subject CN=hsm-prod.example.com and no SAN for `kms.internal.example`. tcpdump shows SYNs from our host but no SYN-ACK back. Here's the tcpdump snippet:
```
13:20:01.123456 IP 192.168.1.10.52344 > 10.12.34.56.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
13:20:01.123601 IP 192.168.1.10.52344 > 10.12.34.56.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
```
No replies.

charlie_eng_infra: if tcpdump shows SYN only, that's a classic egress drop or asymmetric routing. The SNI/cert mismatch you saw could be due to resolving to an external-facing load balancer that terminates TLS with a different cert. Two actionable leads: 
1) Confirm your firewall/NGFW/NAT device allows outbound TCP 443 to the HSM IP range (and preserves source NAT if your HSM allowlist expects a specific SNAT pool).
2) Confirm split-horizon/private DNS zone points to the *internal* load balancer VIP and that the LB forwards TLS passthrough (if HSM expects SNI).

Also check the agent config to ensure kms.endpoint is the internal hostname (not `kms.public.example`). Path misconfig can cause key fetch attempts to the wrong service. See `/etc/redwood/agent.yaml` -> `kms:` section.

bob_customer_sre: our firewall team says we already allow 443 to that CIDR, but they use an upstream proxy that does TLS inspection. Could the proxy rewrite SNI or break the handshake?

charlie_eng_infra: yes, TLS-inspecting proxies will break client cert/SNI expectations unless you do TLS passthrough. HSMs typically require end-to-end TLS. If you have a transparent proxy, either bypass it for the KMS IPs or configure it to allow passthrough for the destination. Also verify the source IP: the HSM may only accept connections from specific SNAT pool; check with your HSM operator for the accepted source range.

dana_security: adding: if the HSM uses client certs, the proxy will also break that. Confirm whether the onboarding required a client cert on the agent side. If so, the agent's TLS client cert must present during handshake — proxy will interrupt that.

oncall-bot: Incident runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-connectivity. Suggested play: collect `tcpdump`, `openssl s_client -servername`, `agent debug` logs, then add temporary allow rule for egress and test.

bob_customer_sre: we checked with the HSM maintainer — they see our SYNs hit their edge LB but return TCP RST to us because the SNI is `kms.internal.example` while their certs are for `hsm-prod.example.com`. They said the correct hostname to use is `hsm-prod.example.com` (internal zone), and our internal DNS was misconfigured to return `kms.internal.example` for historical reasons. We also discovered our upstream proxy was terminating TLS for other domains, but it was bypassed for the HSM CIDR. However, the SNAT pool used by our nodes was not in the HSM allowlist.

alice_support: okay concrete steps to get you to a green state: 
1) Update private DNS so that `kms.internal.example` resolves to the HSM internal VIP AND has the correct RRs so SNI matches the cert (or change agent `kms.endpoint` to `hsm-prod.example.com`).
2) Work with infra/security to add your nodes' SNAT IP(s) to the HSM allowlist (or configure NAT so traffic egresses from the expected SNAT pool).
3) Bypass TLS-inspecting proxy for that destination or configure passthrough.
4) After changes, verify with: `curl -v --resolve 'hsm-prod.example.com:443:10.12.34.56' https://hsm-prod.example.com/health` and `openssl s_client -connect 10.12.34.56:443 -servername hsm-prod.example.com`.

bob_customer_sre: we updated DNS to point `kms.internal.example` -> 10.12.34.56 (private VIP for hsm-prod), added SNAT pool 172.20.0.0/24 to the HSM allowlist, and created a firewall bypass rule for the HSM CIDR. Re-ran the checks and now `openssl` completes and returns the expected cert with CN=hsm-prod.example.com. `curl` returns 200.

Here are the post-change agent logs:
```
2026-02-28T15:03:10Z INFO  redwood.agent.kms: opening TLS connection to hsm-prod.example.com:443
2026-02-28T15:03:10Z INFO  redwood.agent.kms: key fetch successful: key_id=projects/prod/keys/abc123
```

alice_support: awesome, great diagnosis and remediation. Could you confirm app-level errors stopped?

bob_customer_sre: verified — our error rate for KMS 5xx dropped to 0 within 2 minutes and latency is normal. Rolling out the fixes to other regions now. Thanks for the guidance. :tada:

charlie_eng_infra: quick follow-ups for record:
- Root cause: split-horizon DNS returned legacy hostname causing SNI/cert mismatch AND SNAT not configured to match HSM allowlist.
- Mitigation applied: corrected private DNS, added SNAT pool to allowlist, bypassed TLS-inspection for HSM.
- Action items: (a) add a healthcheck alert for `redwood.agent.kms` TLS failures, (b) docs/update runbook with SNAT+DNS checklist for Private deployments, (c) customer to add monitoring for DNS drift.

dana_security: I'll create a short security advisory about TLS-inspection pitfalls with HSMs and circulate with infra teams.

oncall-bot: Closing note: mark resolved when customer confirms full rollout.

bob_customer_sre: marking resolved from our side. leaving traces of commands we used for future teams:
```
# verify DNS -> IP
dig +short hsm-prod.example.com

# verify TLS handshake & cert
openssl s_client -connect 10.12.34.56:443 -servername hsm-prod.example.com -showcerts

# quick HTTP health
curl -v --resolve 'hsm-prod.example.com:443:10.12.34.56' https://hsm-prod.example.com/health

# agent debug logs
sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -f --since "15 minutes ago" | grep kms
```

alice_support: thanks @bob_customer_sre, filing a brief postmortem in support and adding the runbook item. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
